content.title: About
content.content: Pumpkin seeds are the edible seeds of the pumpkin (most often Cucurbita pepo). They come in a tough white hull and as shelled green seeds called pepitas. They have a nutty, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. Pumpkin seeds are eaten as a snack, roasted, and added to salads, porridge, baked goods, granola, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shelled green pumpkin seeds are called pepitas; they have long been eaten in Mexico and Central America.
In Austria, a special pumpkin with seeds that have no hard hull is grown, and a dark green oil is pressed from them.
Seeds can be taken out of a pumpkin at home, rinsed, dried, and roasted.
Pumpkin seeds are crunchy and filling, so they are handy to take along as a snack.
Pumpkin seeds are made into oil, flour, and paste.

items.title: Contain magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contain zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immunity and wound healing.

items.title: Contain iron
items.content: Iron is needed for oxygen transport.

items.title: Source of protein and healthy fats
items.content: The seeds provide plant protein and unsaturated fats.

items.title: Contain antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin E and other compounds protect cells.

items.title: Calories and salt
items.content: Pumpkin seeds are high in calories, and roasted salted ones contain a lot of salt, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Hulls and bloating
items.content: A lot of seeds in the hull are hard to digest and cause bloating and discomfort in some people.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Allergy to pumpkin seeds is possible.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The seeds are not suitable for small children, as they can choke on them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat pumpkin seeds as a snack, or add them to salads, oatmeal, yogurt, smoothies, bread, baked goods, and granola, or grind them for sauces and pesto. To bring out the flavor, lightly toast them in a dry pan. Unsalted seeds are the better choice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store seeds in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long-term storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer, because the fats can turn rancid. Discard seeds that smell rancid or are moldy.
